items.title: 52060_Eddie Barefield oral history interview
items.q: He took me to his piano teacher, a lady named Josephine Guy, that's right. And I started studying piano

ctx.x: Across the street from me lived a fellow who was taking piano, he was about 11 and I was about 9 at the time. He wanted -- we were to be friends, his name was Merle Williams. M-e-r-l-e. He said to me, look, what do you want to be a fighter for? Why don't you play music. I said, you know, I never thought of that things. He said, well, come

on and study piano. He took me to his piano teacher, a lady named Josephine Guy, that's right. And I started studying piano and practicing on his piano because we didn't have a piano at home. I studied piano about a year and was doing pretty good. But the kids in the neighborhood started calling me a sissy because I was playing piano so I didn't want to play the piano, I gave it up. And one day Merle came over to my house and said, they're organizing a community band. And they're going to furnish the instruments…

Well, to please him I went along with him. We went to this meeting and when we got there there was an old man and his name was Mr. Warwick (PHONETIC). He was playing a C melody saxophone. And I had never seen a saxophone before to notice it. And I said, what instrument is that? He said, 'that's a saxophone, C melody.' I said, 'well, that's the instrument I'd like to play.'
